articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure: Definitions, Management, Prognostication, and Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure is a rapidly evolving syndrome characterized by acute decompensation, organ failure, and high short-term mortality. This article reviews international definitions, epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic evaluation, critical-care management, prognostic models, liver transplantation (LT), posttransplant risk assessment, palliative care, current controversies, and emerging research. The recommended clinical approach emphasizes prompt identification of reversible precipitants, evidence-based organ support, serial assessment of disease trajectory during the first week, early referral for LT evaluation when appropriate, and alignment of treatment intensity with prognosis and patient preferences.
articles.authors: Yagan Lina, Mohan Rahul, Hernaez Ruben

articles.title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
articles.abstract: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. It outlines step-wise respiratory support, from high-flow nasal cannula and noninvasive ventilation to lung-protective mechanical ventilation; prevention and treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI), including dialysis options for AKI and end-stage renal disease patients; recognition of hemorrhagic, neurogenic, cardiogenic, and obstructive shock; and secondary complications including coagulopathy, hypothermia, abdominal compartment syndrome, hepatic dysfunction, and hyperglycemia. Ethical triage, palliation, telecritical care, and staffing models are also addressed.
articles.source: The Surgical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Hertel Kristie, Bard Michael

articles.title: Rehabilitation in the Intensive Care Unit: Preparing Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Professionals to Support Biopsychosocial Well-Being.
articles.abstract: With medical advances, more critically ill patients survive and often experience new or worsening physical, cognitive, and/or mental health sequelae. The intensive care unit involves interdisciplinary survival-focused care, and its biopsychosocial impact is profound and long-lasting. In this article, we have highlighted the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning as a person-centered, holistic, and contextually grounded framework for early rehabilitation specifically for critical care survivorship. The goal of this article is to elucidate the key role of physical medicine and rehabilitation professionals in enhancing the recovery trajectory of critical illness survivors within a transdiagnostic, interdisciplinary framework.
articles.source: Physical medicine and rehabilitation clinics of North America
articles.authors: Merbitz Nancy, Hampton Jessica M, Mladen Samantha N, et al.

articles.title: Intraosseous Vascular Access.
articles.abstract: Intraosseous (IO) vascular access is a high-yield bedside procedure for adult inpatient and critical care medicine. When deployed early in high-acuity situations, IO access provides rapid, reliable central vascular access with high success rates and very rare major complications. Effective use requires appropriate site and needle selection, multimodal confirmation of appropriate placement, and vigilant monitoring for extravasation and neurovascular compromise. In awake patients, analgesia, including consideration of IO lidocaine before the initial flush, improves tolerance. IO-derived laboratory results can be useful when no alternative access exists but should be treated as provisional and confirmed once definitive access is secured.
articles.source: The Medical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Voronina Angelina, Freidinger Alexander G, Lords Allie, et al.

articles.title: Prediction, Prescription, and Proactive Medication Management in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: This narrative review examines the evolving role of prediction analytics in comprehensive medication management for critically ill patients. Intensive care unit pharmacotherapy is challenged by medication complexity, physiologic instability, heterogeneous treatment response, and continuous data streams. Predictive systems may support proactive medication management by identifying medication-related harm, therapeutic failure, optimization opportunities, and pharmacist workload earlier in the patient trajectory. The review discusses medication-informed prediction models, prescriptive analytics, workload-aware critical care pharmacist allocation, and potential future applications. Implementation requires actionable predictions, workflow integration, clinician oversight, and attention to equity, safety, and model credibility.
articles.authors: Murray Brian

articles.title: Intensive Monitoring, Big Data, and Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Intensive care is defined by providing a higher level of patient monitoring, but only a fraction of the data created through continuous hemodynamic monitoring are captured in the electronic health record. The monitoring data that is captured misses clinically important deterioration events and is not adequate to represent critical illness physiology for care at the bedside or for research. This article describes the current state of patient monitoring in intensive care, advanced monitors in development, metadata and its role in creating rich intensive care data sources, and machine learning and its current and future applications in intensive care medicine.
articles.authors: Rzewnicki Daniel I, Bhavani Sivasubramanium V

articles.title: Redesigning Intensive Care Unit Workflows: A Learning Health System Approach to Improving Care Delivery.
articles.abstract: Critical care leaders are increasingly asked to improve outcomes, reduce burden, and implement evidence-based care in complex, highly interdependent clinical environments. Meeting this challenge requires redesigning the workflows through which care is delivered, not simply measuring outcomes or adding new tools. This article presents a learning health system model that integrates sociotechnical systems thinking, quality improvement, health services research, and informatics to support workflow redesign. Multidimensional workflow signals inform the Diagnose, Redesign, Implement, Verify, Evolve (DRIVE) cycle to make care delivery more reliable, less burdensome, and better aligned with outcomes that matter to patients.
articles.authors: Murphy David J

articles.title: Optimizing Team Integration of Critical Care Pharmacists: Where We Go Next.
articles.abstract: Critical care pharmacists (CCPs) are essential members of the intensive care unit team who provide comprehensive medication management to improve patient outcomes, safety, and cost efficiency. This article highlights barriers to optimal integration of CCPs within multidisciplinary teams as well as opportunities to address them. Persistent barriers include financial, workforce, data, interprofessional, and regulatory. Strategies to address these gaps may involve standardized metrics, innovative staffing models, and research to strengthen evidence-based implementation. Metrics should include all members of the Stakeholder Triad and should include a mix of workload metrics, safety and efficacy metrics, and work-design metrics.
articles.authors: Smith Susan E, Henry Kelli, Papadopoulos John, et al.

articles.title: Optimizing Team Integration of Critical Care Pharmacists: A History of Critical Care Pharmacy Practice and Evolving Definition of "Optimal Practice".
articles.abstract: Critical Care Pharmacists (CCPs) are essential members of the intensive care unit (ICU) team who provide comprehensive medication management to improve patient outcomes, safety, and cost efficiency. This article highlights best practices for optimal CCP integration, including optimal patient-to-pharmacist ratios, participation in interprofessional rounds, team-based practice models, and expanded coverage across all shifts. The Triple Domain framework is useful to evaluate CCP value across patients, health care teams, and institutions. Best practices include an ICU patient-to-CCP ratio of less than or equal to 15:1 and inclusion of CCPs on daily interprofessional rounds.
articles.authors: Smith Susan E, Bektas Aeryana N, Henry Kelli, et al.

articles.title: The COVID-19 Pandemic as a Stress Test of the Intensive Care Unit Workforce.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic monumentally strained the intensive care unit (ICU) workforce and revealed both the strengths and vulnerabilities in contemporary critical care delivery. In this review, we briefly describe the composition of the US ICU workforce and the organizational features most relevant to staffing. Next, we examine how the pandemic disrupted critical care delivery, specifically health care workers. Finally, we discuss the lasting psychological toll and workforce attrition; highlight adaptations that emerged, such as tele-ICU expansion, virtual family engagement, tiered staffing models, rapid-onboarding curricula, and peer support programs; and outline priorities for policy, practice, and research to strengthen workforce resilience.
articles.authors: Connell Kathryn A, Vranas Kelly C, Yu Hyunmin, et al.

articles.title: The Intensive Care Unit Team: Roles, Scope, and Interprofessional Interdependence in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: A hallmark feature of an intensive care unit (ICU) is the presence of a structured team-based interprofessional model. Although composition of the ICU team varies by organization and patient population, it typically includes critical care nurses, intensivists, respiratory therapists, and clinical pharmacists. Interprofessional teams in ICUs are associated with increased collaboration and improved patient outcomes. However, the ICU team faces challenges in workforce shortages, staffing gaps, and ineffective information sharing, which can inhibit effective team function. Proven strategies to support collaboration among the ICU team include structured interprofessional rounds, strong leadership of the team, care protocols, and quality bundles.
articles.authors: Manzo Laura L, Christoph Ella N I, Kessinger Stephanie K, et al.

articles.title: Streamlining the Evidence-to-Practice Pathway With Computerised Decision Support in Anaesthesiology and Critical Care: A Qualitative Study of Clinician and System-Level Interest Holder Perspectives Across Five Scandinavian Countries.
articles.abstract: Implementing evidence-based recommendations in anaesthesiology and critical care remains challenging due to guideline, workflow and contextual barriers. Guideline-based computerised clinical decision support systems (CDSS), embedded in structured pathways linking international guidelines to Scandinavian-endorsed recommendations and delivered via electronic health records, may help strengthen the evidence-to-practice pathway. This study aimed to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to their use. This qualitative study interviewed 10 clinicians (anaesthesiologists and intensivists; specialists and non-specialists; < 40 and ≥ 40 years; male and female) and nine system-level stakeholders (hospital and health authority representatives) from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. We integrated endorsed international guidelines into a CDSS providing patient-specific reminders linked to recommendations, as well as shared decision-making tools and decision-analytic components. Using a simulation application, participants explored the CDSS in a demo electronic health record. Through a framework analysis based on the GUIDES checklist, we categorised perspectives as barriers, fac
articles.authors: Van de Velde Stijn, Seterelv Siri, Kunnamo Ilkka, et al.

articles.title: A Survey of Clinician-Reported Management of Hypernatremia in the ICU.
articles.abstract: Hypernatremia is frequent in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its prevalence, robust evidence to guide treatment is lacking, and global practice patterns are largely unknown. We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility. This international cross-sectional online survey comprised 20 primarily closed-ended questions, using five-point Likert-scale responses, across four themes: treatment method, threshold, correction rate, and opinion on a proposed trial. Respondents considered a clinical vignette of hypernatremia developing before or during ICU admission, excluding dehydration and chronic causes. It was distributed to ICU physicians worldwide. The survey was sent to 3053 ICU physicians in 17 countries, with 1051 respondents, yielding a response rate of 34%. Of respondents, 74% were consultants, and 26% were residents. The mean ICU experience was 14 years. Increasing free water intake via enteral route was the most frequently reported treatment strategy (80% reporting "often" or "always"). articles.authors: Seitz-Rasmussen Hans Eric Sebastian, Bestle Morten H, Schjørring Olav Lilleholt, et al.

articles.title: Serious Adverse Events in Adult ICU Patients: A Substudy of the PATIENCE Cohort.
articles.abstract: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. We hypothesised that all predefined SAEs would occur in both patients treated and those not treated with prokinetic agents, and that a higher number of SAEs would occur among patients treated with prokinetic agents for more than three consecutive days. This substudy of the inception cohort study "Prokinetic agents in adult intensive care unit patients" included acutely admitted adult ICU patients. The prokinetic agents assessed (exposures) were erythromycin, metoclopramide, domperidone, and prucalopride. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least one episode of five pre-specified SAEs during ICU stay (cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, vomiting with aspiration, diarrhoea, extrapyramidal symptoms). Secondary outcomes were (1) proportion of patients experiencing each SAE, (2) the proportion of patients experiencing any of the SAEs af
articles.authors: Crone Vera, Møller Morten Hylander, Granholm Anders, et al.

articles.title: Discussing Future Treatment and Care in the ICU: Perspectives From Patients.
articles.abstract: Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. However, patients admitted to the ICU are often assessed as incapable of making decisions regarding their care; hence conversations about wishes for treatment are postponed. This study aimed to investigate the experiences of patients who participated in a conversation concerning treatment and care following ICU discharge based on the Danish version of the Recommended Summary Plan for Emergency Care and Treatment (ReSPECT) form. Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with patients who had a conversation about future treatment and care with an intensivist using the ReSPECT form during an ICU admission between November 2024 and July 2025. Relatives who participated in the conversation and were present during the interviews were asked to elaborate on their experiences of the conversation's timing and how they felt about participating in the conversation. articles.authors: Smith Mette A, Zwisler Ann Dorthe, Nissen Anne, et al.

articles.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
articles.abstract: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. However, methods for identifying patients in need of post-ICU support vary widely. As a result, many patients are left without access to established rehabilitation pathways. This consensus recommendation provides a framework for the organisation and content of follow-up for adult ICU survivors in Sweden, informed by available evidence, stakeholder perspectives and expert consensus. The National System for Knowledge-Driven Healthcare Management (NPO) in Sweden commissioned the development of a practice recommendation for the follow-up of critically ill adults. Multidisciplinary experts in ICU survivorship formed a task force group. A systematic literature search in four databases was conducted in 2024 to identify pre-existing systematic reviews on the topic. The literature was reviewed, assessed for quality and recommendations were developed based on the literature evidence. The draft was discussed among multiprofessional groups involved in follow-up, in workshops with critical care nurses (n = 30) and professionals responsibl
articles.authors: Åkerman Eva, Schandl Anna, Ringdal Mona, et al.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction in chronic critical illness: mechanisms, clinical consequences and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Advances in intensive care have improved survival from acute critical illness, leading to a growing population of patients with chronic critical illness (CCI), many of whom require prolonged organ support. This condition is associated with persistent catabolism, inflammation, and poor long-term outcomes. Understanding the metabolic alterations underlying this failure to recover may help identify targets for monitoring and intervention. This review synthesizes current clinical and translational evidence on metabolic dysregulation in CCI and discusses its implications for monitoring, nutritional strategies, and therapeutic interventions. We performed a narrative review informed by a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE followed by manual reference screening. Preclinical, translational and clinical studies addressing energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, autophagy, ketone metabolism, inflammation and recovery trajectories in critical illness were qualitatively synthesized. articles.authors: Castro Sílvia, Granja Cristina, Dionne Joanna C, et al.

articles.title: How are researchers using MIMIC? A sampling-based methods review.
articles.abstract: The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC) database is a widely used open data resource in critical care research. Its accessibility has led to large numbers of research studies being published; however, design and analysis decisions made by individual studies may vary, affecting comparability and reproducibility. We conducted a sampling-based methods review of research that analysed the MIMIC database. Studies published between 2015 and 2025 were eligible for inclusion in the sampling frame. A random sample of 100 eligible studies was identified through the OpenAlex bibliographic database; data were collected using a structured extraction framework. Information was extracted on study aims, cohort definitions, exclusion criteria, outcome specification, handling of missing data, and analytical methods. The review focused on how key design and analytical decisions were reported and justified in the random sample. Studies reported findings from general ICU and specific clinical populations; the study population could not be determined for 32 of the 100 studies. Sixty studies addressed predictive research questions, but only one predictive study reporting external validati
articles.authors: Kenarangi Tayyebeh, Barnett Adrian, Suen Jacky Yung, et al.

articles.title: Analysis of work system components in interprofessional communication to determine shock etiology.
articles.abstract: In critical care settings, lack of agreement among clinicians on shock etiology is associated with higher mortality. Effective interprofessional communication may facilitate agreement on etiology and reduce mortality. This study sought to understand the interaction of work system components (people, environments, tools, tasks) in interprofessional communication to determine shock etiology. We interviewed 28 physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, and pharmacists at three United States hospitals using a Critical Incident Technique. Analysis was guided by the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety model. The principal finding was that clinicians worked across fragmented physical, socio-organizational, and digital environments to balance the urgency to treat shock with intermediate steps to reduce diagnostic uncertainty. The results suggest that future research should acknowledge the benefits of productive disagreement among clinicians and develop supports that promote synchronous communication by bridging physical and socio-organizational fragmentation, compiling and systematizing relevant clinical information, and generating shared awareness among clinicians.
articles.authors: Cong Lixuan, Abahuje Egide, Slocum John D, et al.

articles.title: Training of trainers on medical education reforms: a prospective multicenter French survey among intensivists.
articles.abstract: The recent reform of the second cycle of medical education in France introduced competency-based medical education (CBME) with the incorporation of several pedagogical modalities into undergraduate training and assessment, including objective structured clinical examinations (OSCEs), simulation-based teaching (SBT), and clinical reasoning (CR) instruction throughout the academic year. While these tools are central to preparing competent practitioners, their effective implementation depends on adequately trained educators. We hypothesized that training would be insufficient, notably in the recently introduced pedagogical modalities. We conducted a national, cross-sectional survey (June-September 2023) to assess the level and adequacy of training of board-certified physicians practicing in critical care and involved in undergraduate teaching. An anonymous online questionnaire collected demographic data, teaching frequency, training characteristics, perceived adequacy and usefulness of training, preparedness, and barriers. articles.authors: Hermann Bertrand, Truchot Jennifer, Cariou Alain, et al.

articles.title: Beyond the ICU: family resilience and emotional turmoil after intensive care - a qualitative study.
articles.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, visitation restrictions in ICUs intensified psychological distress among family members, yet the long-term impact of psychosocial support on family resilience remains poorly understood. To evaluate the experiences of family members during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on interactions with healthcare professionals and well-being 18th months after hospitalisation. A qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured interviews with 14 families of patients admitted to the ICU in spring 2020.Data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Experiences were shaped by caring interactions with healthcare professionals, emotional disruption, and reliance on family support. Clear information and psychosocial support fostered trust but were also associated with stress and feelings of isolation. The experience caused profound emotional distress, with family members reporting lasting anxiety, while others described gratitude and personal growth. Support from Family were central to coping, although the responsibility as the primary contact person could increase emotional burden. articles.source: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
articles.authors: Lönnkvist Jenny, Lundberg Tina, Åkerman Eva, et al.

articles.title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with prognosis determined by right ventricular (RV) adaptation to the abrupt rise in pulmonary vascular resistance. Although most cases can be managed outside the intensive care unit, patients with RV failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Management in this setting emphasizes rapid diagnosis and risk stratification, timely initiation of reperfusion therapies, and carefully tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support. Optimal outcomes rely on multidisciplinary collaboration, early escalation of care, and individualized, evidence-based decision-making.
articles.authors: Ehret Jane, Langston Matthew D, Friedman Oren

articles.title: Higher Daily Hospitalization Costs and Intensive Care Utilization Among Decedents With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Bioethical Analysis of End-of-Life Care.
articles.abstract: End-of-life care creates financial burdens. This study examines medical procedures/interventions and costs for inpatients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), comparing those who died during hospitalization to those who survived, analyzing the findings through a bioethical perspective. This observational 1:1 case-control study was conducted at a tertiary care center. Patients with SLE and RA (ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes) who were hospitalized for at least 24 h during two distinct periods-January-June 2019 and January-June 2023-were included. Patients were designated as cases if they died during hospitalization and as controls if they were discharged alive. Data were abstracted from electronic medical records using standardized formats. Microcosting data for each hospitalization were obtained from the accounting department. We identified 29 matched pairs of cases and controls, primarily comprising middle-aged females, with SLE. Cases and controls had similar sociodemographic and disease-related characteristics. articles.source: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
articles.authors: Guaracha-Basañez Guillermo Arturo, Contreras-Yáñez Irazú, Jiménez-Decle Julia Giselle, et al.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and continuous renal replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an important intervention in the treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care, and its application scope continues to expand alongside technological advancements and an increasing patient population. However, in current clinical practice, several factors, including individual patient differences, dynamic treatment needs, and the rational allocation of medical resources, pose challenges to CRRT implementation. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) offers new approaches to address some of these challenges, and its applications in developing decision-support models, refining workflows, and supporting patient communication and education may contribute to more precise and efficient CRRT management. In this article, we discuss the current evidence and potential applications of AI in CRRT, as well as the challenges and strategies for clinical implementation, aiming to provide a reference for future research and clinical translation of AI-assisted CRRT. articles.authors: Li Xiang, Zhang Ling

articles.title: Irritant Contact Dermatitis Related to Fecal and Urinary Incontinence in the Critical Care Population.
articles.abstract: Irritant contact dermatitis due to fecal, urinary, or dual incontinence is a common but often under recognized complication in critically ill patients that contributes to pain, skin breakdown, infection, and pressure injury risk. Despite advances in understanding its prevention and management, practice remains variable. This article contrasts traditional and evidence-based approaches, reviewing terminology, risk factors, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and interventions. A practical critical care application of the Manage→Clean→Protect→Restore care bundle, adapted from the 2026 Wounds International Best Practice Update, is presented to support standardized, proactive incontinence skin care, and improve patient outcomes.
articles.source: Critical care nursing clinics of North America
articles.authors: Hutton Jennifer L

articles.title: Burn Management in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Burn disasters are uncommon but uniquely resource-intensive mass casualty events, requiring prolonged multidisciplinary care that can rapidly exhaust the limited number of verified burn centers and beds. This article reviews the epidemiology and injury patterns of burn disasters, burn-specific triage and transport principles, and system-level planning built on regional burn networks. It examines the American Burn Association's role in center verification, regional response plans, and national burn bed capacity monitoring, alongside federal support mechanisms. Acute resuscitation, damage-control operative strategies, temporary wound coverage, workforce augmentation, and pediatric considerations are addressed, together with ethical decision-making, long-term recovery, and emerging technologies.
articles.source: The Surgical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Khandelwal Anjay, Ozhathil Deepak K

articles.title: Culture and the Intensive Care Unit Team: Factors Driving Teamwork, Safety, Quality, and Well-Being.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) culture and teamwork strongly influence health care quality, patient safety, clinical outcomes, and clinician well-being. Culture shapes how multidisciplinary clinicians communicate, coordinate care, and adopt new practices. Persistent variability in ICU practices, including end-of-life care, sedation management, and mobility, often reflect differences in local culture and team dynamics. Emerging perspectives from complexity science, network science, and behavioral economics conceptualize the ICU as a complex adaptive human network in which collective behavior patterns emerge through repeated clinician interactions. Understanding ICUs through this lens may provide tools, processes, and strategies to improve health care delivery.
articles.authors: Fuchita Mikita, McPeake Joanne, Mikkelsen Mark E

articles.title: Administrative Harm and Workforce Strain Indicators.
articles.abstract: The way work is structured within health care, from work environments to workloads, shapes both the workforce experience as well as job performance. Administrative harm describes the downstream effects of upstream decisions on the design of work itself, impacting workforce well-being and performance, patient care and outcomes, and organizational outcomes. The article reviews current and emerging opportunities to harness digital signals readily available within the electronic health record (EHR), including EHR use metadata and related data sources, to measure, monitor, and predict how work design (job demands and resources) affects workforce, patient, and organizational outcomes.
articles.authors: Leventhal Kara-Grace, Caudill Darren, Moss Marc, et al.

articles.title: Intensive Care Unit Staffing Ratios: Evidence, Experience, Economics, and Execution.
articles.abstract: The clinician-to-patient ratio is a simple construct which can be useful in strategizing for intensive care unit (ICU) staffing. Evidence is limited and inconsistent, but overall suggests such ratios may impact patient outcomes, clinician experiences, and health system economics. Importantly, however, ICU clinicians function as part of an interprofessional team, and no single staffing metric can be considered in isolation. As such, no one-size-fits-all approach to clinician-to-patient ratios exists. Yet, typical ranges are now known and decisions to operate outside of these ranges should be done with care, at least until new evidence can better guide practice.
articles.authors: Gershengorn Hayley B, Buckley Mitchell S, Costa Deena K, et al.

articles.title: Moral Distress, Burnout, and the Intensive Care Unit Environment.
articles.abstract: This article examines the relationship between moral distress and burnout among intensive care unit (ICU) clinicians and argues that moral distress acts as a precursor to burnout. Moral distress arises when clinicians cannot act according to ethical obligations due to systemic constraints, leading to cumulative moral residue. In high-intensity ICU environments, this distress is driven by nonbeneficial treatment, poor communication, and resource limitations. Over time, unresolved moral distress contributes to chronic workplace stress and burnout. The authors emphasize that system-level interventions, particularly ethics consultation and organizational change, are essential to address root causes and improve clinician well-being and patient care.
articles.authors: Epstein Elizabeth G, Bourne Dawn, Taylor Julia F

articles.title: Valvular Shock in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Perioperative Care for Transcatheter Valve Interventions.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease is an uncommon but high-risk cause of cardiogenic shock requiring rapid, multidisciplinary management aimed at bridging patients to definitive surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Early comprehensive Doppler echocardiography is essential, as clinical signs may be subtle. Distinguishing decompensated chronic valvular disease from acute unstable lesions guides urgency and treatment strategy. Medical stabilization and mechanical circulatory support vary markedly between stenotic and regurgitant lesions, and standard shock therapies may be harmful in specific contexts. Transcatheter approaches are preferred when feasible, though their expanding use introduces added complexity in cardiac intensive care.
articles.authors: Prosperi-Porta Graeme, Dahiya Garima, Hibbert Benjamin, et al.

articles.title: Integrating Tummy Time Into Routine NICU Care: Healthcare Workers' Perspectives on Long-Term Implementation in India.
articles.abstract: Prone positioning for play ('Tummy Time') is an evidence-based recommendation that supports early sensory-motor development during infancy. Infants who require neonatal intensive care face a heightened risk of motor developmental delays, underscoring the importance of early developmental care practices. Routine implementation of tummy time remains limited in many settings in India and is not included in national guidelines. Socio-cultural factors further influence the adaptation of such a cost-effective intervention in India. In response, a structured tummy time practice was introduced at discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of a tertiary-care hospital in India in 2016. This study explored multidisciplinary NICU healthcare workers' perspectives on implementing tummy time, including its perceived feasibility, acceptability and long-term integration into routine practice. We conducted in-depth semi-structured interviews with 12 NICU staff members representing varied professional roles. Interviews followed a predefined schedule, they were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated where needed and analysed thematically using MAXQDA software. We identified the f
articles.source: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy
articles.authors: Chutke Amruta, Dholakia Kripa, Bagade Tanmay, et al.

articles.title: Determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract: Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0-1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03-2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44-3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05-3.20) were associated with low QMLT. articles.title: Assessing the consistency of a prognostic transition to persistent critical illness across two U.S. ICU databases: a daily risk-set analysis.
articles.abstract: To test whether an apparent prognostic transition to persistent critical illness persists after daily clinical-state updating. Retrospective daily risk-set analysis using multicenter eICU discovery, single-health-system MIMIC-IV concept replication, cluster-resampled simultaneous inference, and post-primary explanatory updated-state analyses. Two deidentified U.S. critical care databases: eICU Collaborative Research Database v2.0 and MIMIC-IV v3.1. articles.authors: Wu Guoxin, Lv Quankun, Ye Yi, et al.

articles.title: Multidrug-resistant CC3 Staphylococcus haemolyticus with increased vancomycin MIC among neonates in a Brazilian NICU.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus haemolyticus has emerged as a cause of outbreaks in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), particularly involving clonal complex (CC) 3 lineages. We investigated the prevalence and microbiological characteristics of S. haemolyticus colonizing neonates in a Brazilian NICU over two periods, spanning the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Nasal swabs were collected weekly between August 2019-March 2020 and between November 2020-April 2021. Isolates were identified by MALDI-TOF-MS and characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination, SCCmec typing, GTG5-PCR, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST). Among 108 neonates, 75 were colonized by S. haemolyticus and prematurity was the main cause of hospitalization (p=0.03). Colonization rates were similar between periods (71.2% vs. 67.3%; p=0.57), with no clinical or microbiological differences, except for reduced ampicillin-gentamicin use in the second period (p=0.048). articles.title: Therapeutic drug monitoring of meropenem in human serum using a sensitive four-electrode electrochemical biosensor for critically ill patients in intensive care wards.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic drug monitoring of antibiotics in critically ill patients with sepsis remains challenging due to highly variable pharmacokinetics, increasing the risk of under- or overdosing. This paper presents a novel single-use tetrapolar electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) biosensor for the rapid detection of meropenem in human serum. The sensor is based on a gold microband electrode functionalised with a self-assembled monolayer, protein G and anti-meropenem antibodies to enable selective antigen capture and impedance-based quantification. The biosensor demonstrated sensitive detection of meropenem over a range of 1-100 μg/mL in phosphate-buffered saline and within clinically relevant concentrations (8-16 μg/mL) in spiked human serum, with the lowest measured concentration of 1 μg/mL. Binding specificity was validated using tandem mass spectrometry and immunocapture liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. The total assay time was under 15 min. This platform represents a promising approach for rapid, bedside-compatible monitoring of meropenem. articles.title: Early enteral protein intake and respiratory support requirements in critically ill children: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Optimal protein provision during pediatric critical illness remains uncertain, and its relationship with clinically meaningful outcomes is incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate the association between early enteral protein intake and short-term clinical outcomes, with particular focus on respiratory support requirements, in critically ill children. In this retrospective cohort study, children aged 1 month to 18 years who received enteral nutrition for at least three consecutive days in a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit between September 2020 and December 2021 were included. Mean protein intake during the first 72 hours was analyzed both relative to age-based Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) thresholds and as a continuous variable. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were constructed to assess associations between early protein intake and pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) length of stay, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), 28-day ventilator-free days, and requirement for IMV, adjusting for age, illness severity (PRISM III, PELOD), malnutrition status, and energy intake. articles.title: Presepsin outperforms conventional biomarkers for Sepsis diagnosis and 30-day mortality prediction: A multicenter prospective study in a north African ICU cohort.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of intensive care unit (ICU) mortality, necessitating the identification of accurate biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis. Presepsin (sCD14-ST), generated through monocyte/macrophage phagocytosis of bacterial components, offers infection-specific signals. This study compared the diagnostic and prognostic performance of with of procalcitonin (PCT), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-8 (IL-8) within the same patient cohort. This prospective multicenter cohort study enrolled 184 participants across two Algerian tertiary ICUs: 60 healthy controls, 30 patients with pulmonary infection, 46 with sepsis, and 48 with septic shock (Sepsis-3 criteria). All biomarkers were measured using a single blood sample collected within six hours of admission. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC curve analysis and DeLong's test, and independent predictors of 30-day mortality were identified using binary logistic regression. All biomarkers differed significantly between the groups (p < 0.001). articles.title: Clinical practice guideline for renal replacement therapy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (2026 edition).
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and severe complication in critically ill patients, associated with high morbidity and mortality. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is a vital life-support modality for critically ill patients with AKI. However, there remains a lack of unified clinical standards for core issues including the timing of RRT initiation, treatment modality, anticoagulation strategy, and weaning from RRT. In response, the Chinese Society of Critical Care Medicine organized a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop the "Clinical practice guideline for RRT in critically ill patients with AKI (2026 edition)" in accordance with the GRADE approach for grading evidence quality. This guideline was developed through systematic literature retrieval, meta-analysis, and evidence-based medical evidence synthesis, followed by multiple rounds of manuscript review and revision via online and offline meetings of the working group, and final approval by the Standing Committee of the Society. articles.title: Evaluating the prognostic value of admission IL-8 and sST2 as biomarkers of early myocardial injury in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Myocardial injury in severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) is often under-recognized, and interpretation of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) may be complicated by renal dysfunction and critical illness. We evaluated whether admission interleukin-8 (IL-8) and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) could support early risk stratification of guideline-consistent myocardial injury in patients with SCAP. In this prospective cohort of 146 patients with SCAP, guideline-consistent myocardial injury was defined as hs-cTnI elevation above the assay-specific 99th percentile upper reference limit. Admission IL-8, sST2, and their combination were assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and 10-fold cross-validation. Fixed and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-stratified hs-cTnI thresholds were compared in an exploratory analysis. An exploratory subgroup analysis was performed among patients with CURB-65 ≤ 1. The median age was 71 years; 91 patients (62.3%) were male and 55 (37.7%) were female. articles.title: [Emergency medicine requirements for the resuscitation room and the resuscitation room team].
articles.abstract: The resuscitation room is the central interface between prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) and in-hospital emergency care for critically ill and severely injured patients. From an EMS perspective, requirements are defined for activation, prenotification, team structure, handover, overload management and feedback. Written activation and allocation criteria are required that are applicable in the prehospital setting and agreed upon by hospitals, emergency dispatch centres and EMS providers. Prenotification must take place through a continuously available, reliable communication channel, be actively acknowledged and enable transparent feedback on capacity. Paramedics must be authorised to activate the resuscitation room independently of the presence of an emergency physician. On arrival, a qualified and operational team with clearly identifiable roles should be available. Handover should be structured and as interruption-free as possible. The exploratory online survey showed that trauma resuscitation care is predominantly guideline-based and more often includes a written minimum staffing requirement. articles.title: The efficacy and safety of micronutrient complementation in adults during the acute phase of critical illness: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Critically ill patients often experience metabolic imbalances and potentially low micronutrient blood levels that worsen oxidative stress and impair immune function. Despite guideline recommendations, micronutrient complementation is inconsistently applied due to accessibility issues and the lack of validated assessment tools during acute critical illness. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the impact of early intravenous micronutrient complementation on clinical outcomes in ICU patients using real-world electronic medical record data. Adult ICU patients at National Taiwan University Hsinchu Branch from July 2024 to November 2025 who received parenteral nutrition (PN) for at least 24 hours were included. Patients were divided into a treatment group receiving micronutrients within 72 hours of ICU admission and a control group without complementation. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and infectious complications after day 6 of PN; secondary outcomes included ICU/hospital length of stay, inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers, organ support needs, and refeeding syndrome incidence. articles.title: Sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations, 2000-2025: a layered bibliometric and science-mapping analysis.
articles.abstract: We characterised the growth, composition and intellectual structure of sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations from 2000 to 2025, with particular attention to the representation and citation visibility of Nursing-category journals. Web of Science Core Collection Article and Review records retrieved on 1 August 2026 yielded 4760 after deduplication. A deterministic title/author-keyword rule gave a field-central corpus of 1047 nested in an abstract-inclusive corpus of 3588. Two authors independently assessed a 200-record stratified sample. Growth, annual Nursing-category share and citations were modelled using log-linear, binomial logistic and negative binomial regression, respectively. Reporting followed the preliminary guideline for reporting bibliometric reviews of the biomedical literature (BIBLIO). The corpus held 859 Articles and 188 Reviews from 370 sources (29,660 citations; h-index 79), growing 15.30%/year (95% confidence interval [CI] 13.73-16.89). articles.title: The Role of Family Needs in Emotional Distress Among Next of Kin of Critically Ill Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Next of kin of critically ill patients frequently experience distress. Although family needs have been associated with psychological outcomes, their potential role as a pathway linking clinical and relational factors to emotional distress remains poorly understood. To examine whether family needs mediate the relationships between ventilatory support, relationship to the patient and emotional distress among the next of kin of critically ill patients. A cross-sectional study was conducted in an adult Intensive Care Unit in Portugal between September 2024 and February 2025. Emotional distress was assessed using the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scales-21 and family needs using the Family Needs Inventory in the Intensive Care Unit. Mediation analysis was performed using maximum likelihood estimation with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5000 resamples). The study followed the A Guideline for Reporting Mediation Analyses (AGReMA) Statement. Data from 130 critically ill patient-next of kin dyads were analysed. articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are common complications with overlapping metabolic, vascular, and inflammatory pathways. GDM is associated with fetal overgrowth but may also coexist with fetal growth restriction, particularly when placental vascular dysfunction is present. Regional evidence on recorded temporal patterns and joint maternal-neonatal outcomes remains limited in northern China. We analyzed 264,278 eligible singleton deliveries at ≥28 gestational weeks recorded in the Hebei Obstetric Critical Illness Monitoring System across 31 hospitals from 2017 to 2023. Pregnancies were classified as HDP alone, GDM alone, coexisting HDP and GDM, or unaffected. articles.title: Clinical nutrition for critically ill patients: A practical appraisal of guideline gaps and perspectives for future research.
articles.abstract: Malnutrition and accelerated muscle wasting are frequent during critical illness and make nutritional support a central component of ICU care. Nutritional support is therefore central to ICU care, but its optimal timing, route, dose, and composition remain debated. Recent randomized trials have challenged the traditional objective of early full feeding and shifted practice toward progressive, phase-adapted, and tolerance-based nutrition. This narrative review compares current international guidelines for nutritional support in critically ill adults. Guidelines broadly agree that nutrition should be initiated early after clinical stabilization, acute-phase overfeeding should be avoided, energy and protein delivery should be increased progressively, and refeeding syndrome should be anticipated. However, important differences remain regarding acute-phase energy targets, protein dosing, enteral versus parenteral nutrition, supplemental parenteral nutrition, indirect calorimetry, and enriched enteral formulas. articles.title: Pathophysiology-guided nutritional strategies for persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome: an immunometabolic perspective.
articles.abstract: Persistent inflammation, immunosuppression, and catabolism syndrome (PICS) is a phenotype of chronic critical illness characterized by unresolved inflammation, impaired immune competence, sustained catabolism, skeletal muscle loss, recurrent infections, and poor functional recovery. Although guideline-based nutritional support remains fundamental, persistent immunometabolic abnormalities may limit responsiveness to nutrient delivery and contribute to anabolic resistance, impaired substrate utilization, and defective tissue repair. This mini-review examines biological mechanisms limiting nutritional responsiveness in PICS and evaluates evidence for pathophysiology-guided nutritional strategies. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception through September 6, 2026, prioritizing English-language clinical guidelines, clinical studies, and mechanistic or translational evidence relevant to PICS, critical illness, nutritional responsiveness, and immunometabolic nutrition. articles.title: [Correlation between acute kidney injury diagnosed by serum creatinine and urine output criteria and short-term prognosis in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery].
articles.abstract: To analyze the correlation between acute kidney injury (AKI) diagnosed by elevated serum creatinine (Scr) versus only meeting the urine output (UO) reduction criteria and short-term adverse outcomes in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery, and to evaluate the association between even mild elevations in Scr and clinical outcomes furthermore. This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study. A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgery adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Peking University First Hospital from May 20, 2019 to March 7, 2022 were included. According to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline, AKI patients were classified into two groups: the AKI-Scr group (those meeting the Scr elevation criteria) and the AKI-UO group (those fulfilling only the UO reduction criteria). articles.title: Fiber and fluid administration and the risk of constipation in critically ill adults on mechanical ventilation: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Constipation is a common complication in critically ill patients and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the role of enteral nutrition composition, particularly fiber and fluid administration, remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between dietary fiber and fluid administration and constipation in invasive mechanical ventilated critically ill adults. We conducted a prospective cohort study including 74 critically ill adults requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and enteral nutrition. Patients were followed for up to 144 h from initiation of mechanical ventilation. Fiber and total fluid administration were evaluated as time-varying exposures. Constipation was defined as absence of defecation within 144 h. Discrete-time survival analysis was used to assess associations. Constipation occurred in 54% of patients. Time to first defecation ranged from 48 to 504 h. Most patients (97.3%) received early enteral nutrition, although fiber and fluid delivery were frequently below guideline-recommended targets. articles.title: Nutrition management in critically ill surgical patients: a clinical practice guideline appraisal and synthesis.
articles.abstract: Critically ill surgical patients are particularly vulnerable to inadequate nutritional intake due to surgery, trauma, treatment-related interruptions, and hypermetabolic stress. Clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) are important for guiding nutritional management in this population, but specific recommendations remain limited. Therefore, this systematic review aimed to evaluate the methodological quality of CPGs related to nutritional management in critically ill surgical patients and to synthesize their recommendations. Comprehensive bibliographic searches were conducted across six literature databases and ten guideline repositories to identify CPGs published between January 2005 and November 2025. Professional society websites and relevant grey literature sources were also searched. Data on guideline characteristics and development methodology were extracted. The methodological quality of included guidelines was appraised using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II), and the quality of recommendations using the AGREE-Recommendation Excellence (AGREE-REX). articles.title: Individualizing post-ICU nutrition: from guideline intent to bedside practice.
articles.abstract: Survivorship of critical illness has increased, shifting attention toward recovery and long-term outcomes. Post-ICU nutrition is emerging as a clinically relevant, yet underperforming contributor to functional recovery and quality of life. Persistent nutritional inadequacy reflects insufficiently defined physiological requirements and limited implementable evidence-based guidance during ICU recovery. Energy and protein delivery sharply decline after ICU discharge, despite persistent metabolic demands. Underfeeding can result from the absence of recovery-specific targets, patient-level barriers (e.g. appetite loss, dysphagia, fatigue), and fragmented care transitions, including premature feeding-tube removal and suboptimal monitoring of oral intake. Structured patient and family engagement can help operationalize individualized nutritional strategies and improve feasibility without substantial resource burden, acting as continuity agents. Post-ICU nutritional failure reflects combined physiological and implementation challenges. articles.title: ICU-Associated Exposure Keratopathy and Preventable Corneal Blindness: A Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: Exposure keratopathy is an ocular surface injury caused by prolonged corneal exposure, most often from incomplete eyelid closure. Critical illness can intensify exposure through reduced blinking, chemosis, impaired corneal reflexes, sedation, mechanical ventilation, and tear film instability. This narrative clinical review synthesizes contemporary evidence on epidemiology, mechanisms, risk factors, bedside assessment, prevention, protocol implementation, and care in resource-constrained intensive care units (ICUs). PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English language literature from January 2000 through 15 September 2026, supplemented by reference list and guideline searches. Systematic reviews, randomized trials, cohort studies, quality improvement reports, and relevant guidance were prioritized. Pooled evidence indicates that exposure keratopathy is common among critically ill patients, and recent trials support scheduled lubrication, eyelid closure support, and moisture chamber approaches, particularly when the cornea remains exposed. articles.title: Rehabilitation and the post-intensive care syndrome across the recovery continuum: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Improved survival from critical illness has produced a growing population of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors with new or worsened physical, cognitive, and mental-health impairment, defined as post-intensive care syndrome (PICS), and frequent distress among families/caregivers (PICS-family, PICS-F). This narrative review synthesises the evidence in adults treated in high-resource settings. Rather than a formal guideline process, we used a structured descriptive approach: for each recommendation, we identified the predominant study design, assessed the consistency of findings, summarised uncertainties, and assigned an evidence-strength label (high, moderate, low, or insufficient). articles.title: Use of Cystatin C in Tandem with Creatinine to Improve GFR Estimation and Clinical Decision Making.
articles.abstract: Recognizing its clinical utility, the 2024 Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline recommends using equations that integrate serum creatinine and cystatin C for CKD diagnosis and staging. Cystatin C-inclusive equations generally outperform creatinine-based equations in bias and accuracy across diverse populations, including children and patients with comorbidities. Moreover, cystatin C-inclusive equations consistently demonstrate greater prognostic value than creatinine-only equations for clinical outcomes such as kidney failure with replacement therapy, cardiovascular disease, and mortality, particularly in individuals with large differences between creatinine-based and cystatin C-based eGFR. Among hospitalized patients and those undergoing significant changes in muscle mass, such as during weight loss or critical illness, cystatin C may improve GFR estimation and facilitate earlier detection of AKI. In clinical practice, cystatin C informs CKD staging, risk stratification, and medication dosing, particularly in scenarios where creatinine-based equations are less reliable. articles.title: Noninvasive respiratory support for adult patients with acute respiratory failure: an official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline.
articles.abstract: Acute hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure are among the most common reasons for ICU admission and need for invasive mechanical ventilation. Noninvasive respiratory support (NIRS) strategies-including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), noninvasive ventilation (NIV), and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)-may prevent intubation, improve outcomes, and reduce ICU utilization. However, there is uncertainty regarding optimal patient and modality selection, resulting in variable implementation. There are no clinical practice guidelines comprehensively addressing the use of the different NIRS strategies across the spectrum of acute respiratory failure. To update and develop new evidence-based clinical practice recommendations informing NIRS use, including HFNC, NIV and CPAP, in adults with acute respiratory failure. A multidisciplinary panel used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to address four PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome) questions related to the use of NIRS for hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure, preoxygenation for intubation, and postextubation respiratory support.
